narration.text: The property tax protest, with comparable sales. This is a chore for a Texas couple with their home, a rental duplex and a vacant lot, and four appraisal notices in the mail. Read each notice of appraised value and work out its deadline. Athena works it across 4 portals: Mailnest, Deedvault, Compsmith sales and Countyline Appraisal. On the bench, she found 5 of 8 eligible items, worth 1,470 dollars of the 2,310 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 9 traps, and she walked past 9. Among them: A vacant lot whose comparable sales come out above its notice: the value is fair, so there is nothing to protest. A condo sold last November, whose notice still came: the couple did not own it on January 1. She took 4 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 4 hours, so she was about 55 times faster. The verdict: short. Found 64% of the value, expected 75%; found 5 of 8 items, expected 75%. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
